name: magics
why: ECMWF weather plotting software is real atmospheric science you can run at home, though it is heavy and niche.

brief.what_it_is: Magics is ECMWF's meteorological plotting software, used to draw weather and climate maps and graphs. It is reached through Python or Fortran interfaces or through Metview. It plots contours, wind fields, observations, satellite images, symbols, text, axes and graphs including boxplots. Input can be GRIB 1 and 2 (read via ECMWF's ecCodes), gaussian, regular and fitted grids, BUFR, NetCDF, or ODB databases. Output can be PostScript, EPS, PDF, GIF, PNG or SVG.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage presents it as ECMWF's own plotting tool for meteorological data, offered as a standalone option alongside the Metview environment.
brief.how_it_works: The homepage says data is read through ECMWF's ecCodes library for GRIB, with other formats handled directly. It describes Magics as a library with Python and Fortran interfaces, so a script builds a plot from these pieces and writes it to one of the output formats. The homepage also says Magics uses the Terralib library in cooperation with Brazil's INPE.
brief.install_notes: The GitHub README lists installation through PyPI (package name Magics) or conda (conda-forge, package magics), a Docker image on DockerHub (ecmwf/magics), and a Binder notebook gallery. The README sends readers to a separate Installation Guide for compiling from source. The homepage links to release tarballs (Magics-4.x-Source.tar.gz), and its text says Magics must be compiled and installed to build from source. The pages I read did not describe hardware, accounts, or first-run configuration.
brief.standout: It handles many meteorological data formats natively, including GRIB via ecCodes, and it is the plotting engine underneath ECMWF's Metview. The Binder notebook gallery makes it possible to try it without installing anything.
brief.status: Maintained, judging by the release list on the homepage. Its most recent entry is Magics-4.17.1 (listed as Oct 15, 2026), preceded by 4.16.0 on Apr 10, 2025 and 4.15.5 on Nov 22, 2024. The Confluence page itself was last updated Nov 09, 2023. The GitHub README shows CI badges for Linux, macOS and Windows, but I did not check commit history.
brief.caveats: The homepage is a Confluence wiki page, and the fetch was cut off at 40,000 characters, so I did not see the rest of it. The GitHub README points to an external Installation Guide I did not open, and it is thin: it has badges, package-manager pointers and a license, with no usage examples. The scout note calls it heavy and niche, and the pages show a compiled tool with several library dependencies (ecCodes, Terralib). The executable names in the brew metadata (magics, metgram, magml and others) do not appear in either page, so I could not confirm what they do. The README's copyright line reads 1996-2019, though the license is Apache 2.0.
quotes: Magics is ECMWF's meteorological plotting software and can be either accessed directly through its Python or Fortran interfaces or by using Metview.
The tarballs below are released under Apache License 2.0.
Magics uses the Terralib library in cooperation with Brazil's INPE.
